outcome: weight gain from birth to discharge
cohort: The study included 642 preterm infants from a single center in Hong Kong, with gestational age less than 37 weeks and birth weights less than 2200 g, categorized into low birth weight (LBW) and very low birth weight (VLBW) groups.
finding: LBW infants fed breast milk had better growth z-scores and lower SGA status at discharge compared with those predominately fed preterm formula.
birth_weight: Less than 2200g (466 LBW infants: >=1500g and <2200g; 176 VLBW infants: <1500g)
